headline: Legal action to be taken over harassment of Prof Yunus: PM’s information adviser

members.title: Legal action to be taken over harassment of Prof Yunus: PM’s information adviser
members.lead: Legal action will be taken over the harassment of Professor Muhammad Yunus, chief adviser to the former interim government, in the United States, said Zahed Ur Rahman, the prime minister’s adviser on information and broadcasting. He said the same legal process would be followed as in the case of actress Azmeri Haque Badhon, who was harassed in Italy. Speaking at a regular press briefing at the Secretariat on the government’s activities, Zahed Ur Rahman made the remarks on Tuesday in response to journalists’ questions about the alleged harassment of Yunus. . A video of the incident on Monday has circulated widely on social media. It shows Yunus being taken out of New York’s John F Kennedy International Airport in a wheelchair as several people approach him and shout slogans. The protesters can be heard yelling “Why you come here?” and making other derogatory remarks directed at him. Several expatriate supporters of the Awami League (whose activities have been banned in the country) have been accused of harassing Muhammad Yunus. Responding to questions about the incident at Tuesday’s briefing, the information adviser said, “Of course, those committing this offence will face action. I am aware of the legal process initiated after our actress (Azmeri Haque Badhon) was harassed. The same will happen in this case.” . “I want to tell the Awami League goons living in different parts of the world that if they try to take such steps, they will not go unchallenged. There is no question of that,” he added. Actress Badhon was harassed in Italy last month. The information adviser also said the government would investigate whether Muhammad Yunus had received the protocol and dignity he was entitled to as a former chief adviser. . Asked about political reconciliation, Zahed Ur Rahman cited the lack of remorse among leaders of the Awami League (whose activities have been banned in the country) and the threats they had made on various occasions. members.title: Harassing Prof Yunus has exposed the character of Awami League: Nahid Islam
members.lead: Nahid Islam, Chief Whip of the Opposition in the National Parliament and convener of the National Citizen Party (NCP), has strongly condemned and protested the incident in which Professor Muhammad Yunus, former chief adviser of the interim government, was harassed at a US airport. He said the attempt to harass Professor Yunus at John F Kennedy International Airport in the United States has once again exposed the brutal, violent, and inhuman nature of Awami League’s (whose activities are banned) terror-dependent politics. . Nahid Islam made these remarks in a statement sent to the media today, Tuesday. A video of the incident, in which Professor Yunus was harassed as he left New York’s airport in a wheelchair last Monday, has circulated on social media. The video shows several people approaching Professor Yunus and shouting slogans at him in loud voices. At the time, the protesters were shouting various accusatory and insulting remarks directed at him, including “Why did you come here?” and “Go back.” Several expatriate supporters of Awami League, whose activities are banned, have been accused of harassing him. . Nahid Islam described the incident as an “attempt by fascist terrorists” and said that even two years after being decisively rejected by the people of Bangladesh, there has been not the slightest change in the character of the Awami League’s terrorist forces. There is not even the slightest sign of remorse among them for their past misdeeds. “This terrorist network, active both at home and abroad, must be completely thwarted. The trials of those involved in enforced disappearances and killings during the fascist era, including the July massacre, must be completed and the verdicts swiftly implemented. In addition, the trial of the Awami League as a political party must begin immediately on charges of genocide and terrorism,” he said.
